previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of chronic systolic and diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for acute decompensated heart failure characterized by worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and fluid overload. The exacerbation was likely triggered by dietary indiscretion and suboptimal rate control. He was treated with IV and then oral furosemide, resulting in weight loss from 342 to 329 pounds, improved symptoms, and resolution of tachycardia and edema. His warfarin was adjusted to correct a subtherapeutic INR, and beta-blocker therapy was optimized. Despite clinical improvement, the patient left against medical advice before completing medication optimization or receiving formal discharge instructions. He agreed to follow up with his primary care provider and pursue outpatient evaluation for obstructive sleep apnea.

Ostium secundum type atrial septal defect
Personal history of noncompliance with medical treatment, presenting hazards to health
